response.content: {"visual":{"fullPrompt":"Wide handheld cinematic night frame, modern social-first editorial campaign energy, 16:9. SCARLETT VEGA wears a fitted black cotton turtleneck with sleeves pushed up to the elbows, dark slim jeans, scuffed black ankle boots, and a slouchy dark denim-canvas jacket, with a heavy natural-canvas tote bag slung over one shoulder, small gold hoop earrings and a thin silver ring on her right index finger, glossy coral lips catching the light. She is caught mid-stride jogging across a striped crosswalk against the countdown, weight forward on the ball of one boot, jacket hem lifting, tote swinging out from her hip, torso twisting as she looks back over her shoulder directly into the lens with a grin — pure potential energy, one breath before the next step lands. The environment is a wide crosstown midtown avenue at night: yellow taxis stacked nose-to-tail and idling, headlights blooming into flare across the frame, exhaust and a plume of manhole steam drifting through the beams, a pedestrian countdown signal glowing red at the curb edge, wet-slick asphalt smearing reflections of yellow, white and red into long streaks along the painted crosswalk stripes, and a towering wall of illuminated glass-and-steel office facade glowing cool white behind, its lit floors receding into soft bokeh. Lighting is entirely mixed practical night sources — hard headlight key raking from camera-left, cool office glass backlight carving a crisp rim along her shoulders and jawline, warm streetlamp spill overhead, red signal accent bouncing off wet ground; crisp true-to-life color grade, warm natural skin tones, lifted airy shadows, taxi yellow and coral popping against deep navy-black.
